---
title: "Exercise 2 · Git with an Agent"
subtitle: "Ship a change through branch → commit → pull request → merge"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Time:** ~15 min · **Pairs with:** [Git & GitHub](../git-github.qmd) · **Goal:** run the core control loop end-to-end, so you trust an agent with real code.
:::

We'll continue in the `agentic-ex1` folder from Exercise 1 (or make a fresh one). By the end you'll have a change reviewed and merged through a real pull request.

## 1 · Make it a repo and put it on GitHub (3 min)

```bash
cd agentic-ex1          # or your Exercise 1 folder
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial synthetic-data scripts"
gh repo create agentic-ex1 --private --source=. --push
```

`gh repo create` makes the GitHub repo and pushes `main` in one step. (Use `--private` for a throwaway.)

## 2 · Branch for the change (1 min)

Never work on `main`. Ask the agent — or type it yourself:

```bash
git switch -c feature/add-summary-table
```

Or say to Claude Code: *"Create a branch called `feature/add-summary-table` and work there."*

## 3 · Direct the change, in small commits (5 min)

Give the agent a real task and have it commit as it goes:

```text
On this branch: add a script `table.R` that writes a summary table of
mean and SD of cost by treatment arm to tables/summary.csv. Show me the
diff, then commit it with a clear message.
```

Review what it shows you. Then:

```text
Also add a one-line note about this table to the README, and commit that
separately.
```

Check your history:

```bash
git log --oneline
```

You should see two small, clearly-labelled commits.

## 4 · Open a pull request (2 min)

```bash
git push -u origin feature/add-summary-table
gh pr create --title "Add cost summary table" --fill
```

Or let the agent do it: *"Push this branch and open a pull request into main."*

## 5 · Review the diff — the gate (2 min)

This is the whole point. **Read the change before you accept it:**

```bash
gh pr diff
```

Ask yourself: is this *only* what I asked for? Any surprise edits? Right files?

::: {.callout-tip}
## Practice catching something
Before merging, ask the agent to *"add a totals row to the summary table."* Re-run `gh pr diff` and find that new change in the diff. Seeing your review surface update is the muscle you're building.
:::

## 6 · Merge what you approve (1 min)

```bash
gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch
git switch main && git pull
```

Your approved change is now on `main`; the branch is cleaned up; `main` never saw the messy middle.

## You're done when…

- [ ] Your repo is on GitHub with `main` pushed.
- [ ] You made a change on a **branch**, in at least two small commits.
- [ ] You opened a **pull request** and ran `gh pr diff` to review it.
- [ ] You **merged** it and returned to a clean `main`.

::: {.callout-warning}
## If something breaks
- `gh: not authenticated` → run `gh auth login` (see [Setup](../setup.qmd)).
- Pushed to the wrong branch? You're on a throwaway repo — safe to experiment. Try `git switch main` and start the branch again.
- **Don't** run `git push --force` or `git reset --hard` to "fix" things right now — ask a facilitator first.
:::
